verbalization: Glasdegib is implicated in the treatment of Acute Myeloid Leukemia (AML) with T(8;21)(q22;q22) translocation through a mechanism involving the NPM1 somatic mutation. This relationship is supported by the shared indication of Enasidenib and Quizartinib, both of which are known to target AML with NPM1 mutations. The evidence suggests that Glasdegib may act through a similar mechanism, potentially by inhibiting enzymes involved in the metabolic pathways that are dysregulated in AML with NPM1 mutations. The presence of multiple pathways leading to the same final indication reinforces the likelihood of a shared therapeutic target. The integration of these paths highlights the potential for Glasdegib to be a relevant treatment for this specific AML sub-type, though further mechanistic studies are needed to confirm the exact relationship.
